rv.q: Cry/Laugh is neither funny enough to carry the meandering story and its absurdist twists, nor focused enough to articulate its political intent.

Their plight says much about a world that would rather tune in to assorted gizmos, gadgets and other latter-day devil’s handiwork than make the effort required for some good old-fashioned face-to-face time. This is the case even if their surreal flights of fancy lead them up the garden path and back again somewhat.
The wild and wonderful ending is fantastic – it’s just a shame it takes forty minutes to get there.

cn.t: Dhanak's medieval tale of a town crier and jester exploring power dynamics receives mixed reviews, with critics finding the premise intriguing but execution uneven across this lunchtime Play, Pie, and Pint production.
